description: Mappings between AI threat catalogs and requirements, restricted to statements published by an authoritative source. One row = one published link; nothing is composed or inferred. Direction is as published (source → target). Filter by 'authority' and 'status' before display: 'final' rows come from final publications or data releases, 'draft' rows from NIST drafts, 'superseded' rows from the OWASP LLM Top 10 2025, and 'unreviewed' rows from the OWASP GenAI Security Crosswalk, whose own schema marks them as not reviewed by a named person.
license: Mixed. Identifiers and relationships are facts. Row 'text' fields are verbatim from the authority's publication and keep its license (see authorities[].license): ATLAS texts Apache-2.0 (© MITRE); OWASP texts CC BY-SA 4.0 (attribution to the OWASP GenAI Security Project; adaptations must be shared alike); NIST texts public domain.

relationships.mitigates: ATLAS mitigation → ATLAS technique; text = the mitigation's use for that technique
relationships.attack-reference: ATLAS object → the MITRE ATT&CK object it references ('attack-reference')

owasp-llm-top10-2026.name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026 (v1.0), Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings
owasp-llm-top10-2026.notes: Coarse-level mappings (ATLAS and ATT&CK tactics, AI RMF categories, AI 600-1 risk categories, CWE, CSA AICM domains, AIVSS core risks, OWASP ASI/DSGAI entries), each marked primary (●) or supporting (○), pinned to the framework versions in 'Framework Sources & Versions' (ATLAS content v2026.06: tactic AML.TA0001 is printed as 'AI Attack Staging', renamed 'AI Attack Adaptation' in ATLAS 2026.08).

owasp-llm-top10-2025.name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025, 'Related Frameworks and Taxonomies' sections
owasp-llm-top10-2025.notes: Technique-level ATLAS references written against ATLAS 4.x (2024): several names have since changed ('ML' → 'AI'); targetNameNow gives the 2026.09 name. Framework-level references without an element identifier are listed under 'excluded'.

owasp-agentic-top10-2026.name: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026, Appendix A - OWASP Agentic AI Security Mapping Matrix
owasp-agentic-top10-2026.publisher: OWASP GenAI Security Project — Agentic Security Initiative
owasp-agentic-top10-2026.notes: Maps ASI entries to OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 entries, OWASP Agentic AI Threats & Mitigations T-codes and AIVSS core risks (named without identifiers; id is null). No ATLAS or NIST mapping is published for the Agentic Top 10.

nist-ir-8596-iprd.name: NIST IR 8596 iprd, Cybersecurity Framework Profile for AI (Cyber AI Profile) — Example Informative References
nist-ir-8596-iprd.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
nist-ir-8596-iprd.license: Public domain — U.S. Government work (17 U.S.C. §105)
nist-ir-8596-iprd.notes: CSF 2.0 subcategory → MITRE ATLAS mitigation / 'OWASP LLM Top Ten: LLM03 Supply Chain' (the 2025 edition was current when the draft was written), per focus area (Secure, Defend, Thwart). NIST: 'This preliminary draft reflects examples of Informative References.' References that cite ATLAS or NIST AI 100-2e2025 as a whole are listed under 'excluded'. The rows are cross-checked against the independent extraction corpus/nist-ai-rmf/cyber-ai-profile.json (tools/reports/mappings-report.json, crossChecks).

nist-cosais-outline.name: NIST SP 800-53 Control Overlays for Securing AI Systems (COSAiS): Using Predictive AI — draft annotated outline
nist-cosais-outline.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
nist-cosais-outline.license: Public domain — U.S. Government work (17 U.S.C. §105)
nist-cosais-outline.notes: Tailored SP 800-53 control → 'Relevant NIST AI 100-2e2025 Attack ID'. Control IDs normalised from the zero-padded form (AC-06, SA-11(02)); 'NIST AML.011' normalised to NISTAML.011.

nist-ai-100-2e2025.name: NIST AI 100-2 E2025, Sec. 3.3.3 Mitigations (direct prompting attacks) — citations of ATLAS mitigations

nist-ai-100-2e2025.license: Public domain — U.S. Government work (17 U.S.C. §105)
nist-ai-100-2e2025.notes: The 'Usage restrictions' mitigation for NISTAML.018 cites ATLAS AML.M0000-M0002 and AML.M0004 as sources.

owasp-genai-crosswalk.name: OWASP GenAI Security Crosswalk (OWASP GenAI Security Project — GenAI Data Security Initiative), v4.0.0 + main @ 922350d
owasp-genai-crosswalk.license: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Copyright (c) 2026 OWASP GenAI Data Security Initiative)
owasp-genai-crosswalk.notes: Listed as an OWASP GenAI Security Project resource (2026-09-01). Its rows carry confidence 'unreviewed' (no named reviewer, per its own schema v2). Checks found identifier/label mismatches (e.g. AI RMF IDs written GV-1.7 with labels that do not describe that subcategory; CSF 'PR.PS-04' used for secure development). Excluded: all of Agentic_FedRAMP.md (keyed to ASI titles that are not the published list) and the 17 ATLAS rows the crosswalk itself marks '**DRAFT — not an ATLAS technique name [or id]; retarget pending SME review (#93)**'. Use only as a lead, never as an authoritative requirement link.

mappings.text: Canonical crosswalk baseline mapping — ASI09 lists Improper Output Handling as a contributing LLM risk. The content match is loose: this entry's scenarios are machine-to-machine (unvalidated output reaching a shell, browser, or database), while ASI09 concerns deceiving a human operator; the shared thread is unvalidated model output reaching a downstream trust decision.

target.label: DSGAI12 — Unsafe Natural- Language Data Gateways (LLM-to-SQL/Graph)

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — OWASP GenAI Data Security 2026 (DSGAI), row LLM10
mappings.text: LLM-generated SQL executed without parameterization or scrutiny reaches the database directly and can delete entire tables.

target.label: DSGAI06 — Tool, Plugin & Agent Data Exchange Risks

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — OWASP GenAI Data Security 2026 (DSGAI), row LLM10
mappings.text: Unvalidated model output crosses into a downstream tool or extension for execution.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — OWASP GenAI Data Security 2026 (DSGAI), row LLM10
mappings.text: Unescaped output rendered by a client encodes and sends conversation data to an attacker-controlled server, as in image-URL exfiltration.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — OWASP GenAI Data Security 2026 (DSGAI), row LLM10
mappings.text: Client renderers such as chat UIs, IDEs, and email clients auto-fetch external resources from raw model output, executing the exfiltration.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE ATLAS, row LLM10
mappings.text: Unvalidated model output passed to a shell, browser, or SQL interpreter executes adversary-controlled code, yielding command execution, cross-site scripting, or SQL injection.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE ATLAS, row LLM10
mappings.text: Model output encoded and sent to an attacker server, or embedded in a Markdown-image URL, carries sensitive data out of the application.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE ATLAS, row LLM10
mappings.text: Unhandled output reaching a privileged sink can delete database tables or force a downstream service offline.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE ATLAS, row LLM10
mappings.text: When the model holds privileges beyond the end user, unvalidated output reaching a privileged sink escalates those privileges to the attacker.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE ATT&CK, row LLM10
mappings.text: Passing unvalidated model output into shell, eval, or database interfaces yields remote code execution, cross-site scripting, and SQL injection on backend systems.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE ATT&CK, row LLM10
mappings.text: Model output encodes sensitive conversation data and sends it to an attacker-controlled server, including via markdown-image URLs.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE ATT&CK, row LLM10
mappings.text: Unscrutinized model-generated SQL deletes database tables and a privileged extension is driven to shut down, causing data destruction and loss of availability.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE ATT&CK, row LLM10
mappings.text: When the application grants the model privileges beyond those intended for end users, unhandled output enables escalation of privileges.

target.label: CWE-1426 Improper Validation of Generative AI Output

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE CWE (Common Weakness Enumeration), row LLM10
mappings.text: Model output is passed downstream with insufficient validation, sanitization, or handling, the entry's exact subject.

target.label: CWE-116 Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE CWE (Common Weakness Enumeration), row LLM10
mappings.text: Missing context-aware output encoding across HTML, JavaScript, SQL, and terminal sinks is the root cause.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE CWE (Common Weakness Enumeration), row LLM10
mappings.text: Cross-site scripting is the most-repeated concrete sink, addressed by content-security-policy and output-encoding defenses.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE CWE (Common Weakness Enumeration), row LLM10
mappings.text: The neutralization pillar covers control-character sanitization of ANSI, BEL, OSC, backspace, and carriage-return sequences and SQL escaping and parameterization.

target.label: CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE CWE (Common Weakness Enumeration), row LLM10
mappings.text: Unhandled output leaks sensitive conversation and website content to an attacker.

target.label: CWE-201 Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — MITRE CWE (Common Weakness Enumeration), row LLM10
mappings.text: Sensitive data is smuggled into the hostname or query string of an auto-fetched Markdown-image request.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile), row LLM10
mappings.text: Unhandled model output flows into downstream systems as remote code execution, XSS, SQL injection, SSRF, CSRF, and privilege escalation.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile), row LLM10
mappings.text: Unsanitized output can leak sensitive conversation data to an attacker.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile), row LLM10
mappings.text: Generated code can reference hallucinated nonexistent software packages, a confabulation facet of unsafe output.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile), row LLM10
mappings.text: Third-party extensions that fail to validate inputs and hallucinated-package installs implicate component integration and supply chain.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — CSA AI Controls Matrix (AICM), row LLM10
mappings.text: Validates model responses as untrusted input and applies context-aware output encoding, parameterized queries, and content-security policy before outputs reach downstream interpreters.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — CSA AI Controls Matrix (AICM), row LLM10
mappings.text: Logs and monitors model outputs so exploitation patterns in downstream handling are detected.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — CSA AI Controls Matrix (AICM), row LLM10
mappings.text: Treats the model as any other user under a zero-trust posture so its outputs never inherit privileges beyond the end user.

target.label: AIVSS-7 Insecure Agent Critical Systems Interaction

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — OWASP AIVSS (AI Vulnerability Scoring System), row LLM10
mappings.text: Unvalidated model output reaching a shell, exec/eval, SQL, or file-path sink yields remote code execution, SQL injection, or path traversal on backend systems.

mappings.locator: Appendix A: Related Framework Mappings — OWASP AIVSS (AI Vulnerability Scoring System), row LLM10
mappings.text: A general-purpose LLM's unvalidated response passed to a privileged extension causes the extension to be misused, for example forced into an unintended shutdown.

mappings.text: Encrypt training data, fine-tuning datasets, and model weights at rest; prevent data memorisation exposure through access controls on data stores

mappings.text: Enforce role-based access control on model inference endpoints; restrict access to training data, fine-tuning data, and model configuration based on clearance and need-to-know

mappings.text: Enforce least privilege for all AI agent tool access, API permissions, and autonomous action scope; restrict to minimum capabilities needed per deployment

mappings.text: Restrict AI systems to minimum necessary capabilities; disable unused tools, APIs, and action types; enforce capability restrictions in configuration
